original_source_binding.abstract_tex:
We give negative answers to the two slit-monotonicity questions of
P.~L.~Duren recorded as Problem~6.72 in Hayman--Lingham.
Every global maximizer of the real part of
\(a_2+i10^{-24}(a_4-3a_3)\) in the normalized schlicht class
omits an arc with nonmonotone continuous argument and nonmonotone radial
angle, under both signed and ordinary unsigned conventions.
The proof uses classical support-point geometry, a quantitative area-theorem
estimate for the actual slit tip, and controlled inversion of the
Schiffer differential. It establishes actual extremizers by compactness
and does not assume that an arbitrary trajectory is an extremal slit.
No formula for the maximizing function or uniqueness is required.
This is an unrefereed AI-assisted research note.

original_source_binding.abstract_tex: For two independent standard fractional Brownian motions with the same fixed Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1)$, we give a localized Gaussian-witness proof that every square-integrable estimator of the canonical iterated integral $X_T=\int_0^T B^1_s\,dB^2_s$, based on both complete uniform grids of $n$ observations on $[0,T]$, has root mean-square error at least $c_HT^{2H}n^{1/2-2H}$. The positive constant is explicit and depends only on $H$; the inequality holds for every $T>0$ and integer $n\ge1$, including nonlinear estimators. Smooth compactly supported covariance paths, a Fourier periodization upper Gram bound, and an exact deterministic area pairing provide the witness. The Brownian optimum and the smooth asymptotic rate are prior results. Fourier localization and Gaussian projection have established antecedents; historical theorem and method priority, full novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain unverified. The note uses canonical-area existence and sufficient $L^2$ convergence, without endorsing exact Euler-error coefficients of the pinned arXiv v1.
